The increase in net interest income was mainly due to higher average deposit spreads and volumes, partially offset by higher mortgage funding costs.

comparisons.peer_summary: 2024 net revenues were driven by higher average credit card and deposit balances in Consumer platforms, partially offset by lower transaction banking revenues due to the sale of the seller financing loan portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS discuss the mixed drivers of transaction-related banking revenues, specifically highlighting the role of deposit balances. BAC's Global Transaction Services revenue declined due to higher deposit costs, partially offset by higher average deposit balances. GS's Platform Solutions (which includes transaction banking) saw lower revenues primarily due to the sale of a loan portfolio, while its Consumer platforms saw higher revenues driven by higher average deposit balances. Both firms identify higher average deposit balances as a positive volume driver for transaction/consumer revenue, even as other factors (costs for BAC, portfolio sales for GS) negatively impacted total revenue.

sentences.text: Global Transaction Services revenue decreased $911 million in 2024 compared to 2023 primarily driven by higher deposit costs, partially offset by the benefit of higher average deposit balances and treasury service charges.

Notwithstanding our strategic decision to narrow the focus on consumer-related activities, Consumer platforms net revenues were slightly higher compared with 2023, reflecting higher average credit card balances and higher average deposit balances, largely offset by the impact of the planned transition of the GM credit card program to another issuer.
Transaction banking and other net revenues were lower, primarily reflecting lower net revenues related to the seller financing loan portfolio that was sold during 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income increased, driven by balance sheet actions including reinvestments in investment securities, higher revolving card balances, the timing impact of First Republic, higher wholesale deposit balances, and higher Markets net interest income, largely offset by deposit margin compression and lower average deposit balances in CCB.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM explicitly cite 'deposit margin compression' or 'higher deposit costs' as key headwinds to revenue growth in their respective segments. BAC attributes its Global Transaction Services revenue decline to higher deposit costs. JPM attributes offsetting factors for its net interest income increase to 'deposit margin compression across the lines of business.' Both disclosures reflect the industry-wide pressure of rising deposit costs eroding net interest margins or service revenues.

MS's Wealth Management net interest revenue decreased 10% primarily due to lower average sweep deposits. While the specific drivers differ (costs vs. volume of sweep deposits), both disclosures highlight a reduction in revenue from deposit-related activities, illustrating sensitivity to deposit behavior and pricing in transaction/wealth banking services.
